priorStories.headline: World court finds Myanmar committed Rohingya genocide
priorStories.body:
The International Court of Justice ruled that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya during military operations in northern Rakhine State in 2017. It also found that Myanmar failed to prevent and punish genocide.

The court ordered Myanmar to investigate and prosecute those responsible, facilitate safe and voluntary returns, restore property and provide compensation. The judgment determines Myanmar’s responsibility as a state; it does not convict individuals of crimes.

sources.name: International Court of Justice — press release hosted by UNHCR Refworld
UN Independent Investigative Mechanism for Myanmar

candidates.summary: The Office for National Statistics released October retail figures showing that sales volumes in Great Britain rose 0.7% from September and 2.3% from a year earlier. Volumes increased 0.4% over the three months to October compared with the preceding three months. Supermarkets reported increased purchases of long-life food following the government's Be Ready campaign; clothing sales also strengthened.
candidates.title: Great Britain retail sales rose 0.7% in October, official figures show

candidates.summary: Taiwan's Taiex closed Friday down 6.2% at 36,033.29, bringing its weekly decline to 17.5%. South Korea's Kospi closed down 5.2% at 4,869.96, while Japan's Nikkei 225 fell 5.1% to 56,436.65. Technology and semiconductor shares were among the largest decliners.
candidates.title: Taiwan, South Korea and Japan stock indexes close sharply lower

candidates.summary: Polish officials said three Russian objects, believed to be two missiles and a jet-powered drone, entered Polish airspace and came down in southeastern Poland on November 20. Prime Minister Donald Tusk described the incident as an apparent intentional provocation coinciding with European military exercises for a possible postwar mission in Ukraine. The identification of all three objects remained preliminary.
candidates.title: Poland reports Russian airspace violations during European military exercises

candidates.summary: Estonia's government decided on November 20 to close road border crossings with Russia from December 1, citing Russian hostile activities. The suspension is planned for at least six months, after which the government will decide whether to extend it. Russia's Foreign Ministry criticized the decision and threatened political and diplomatic responses. The crossings had not closed under this decision at the time of reporting.
candidates.title: Estonia decides to close road border crossings with Russia from December 1

candidates.summary: Iraqi security forces established a command headquarters on the outskirts of Jurf al-Sakhar on November 20, entering a longtime stronghold of the Iran-backed Kataib Hezbollah militia. Two Iraqi officials told AP that an agreement allowed security forces to enter without an immediate militia withdrawal. The deployment included army, federal police, energy-sector police and Popular Mobilization Forces personnel; the agreement envisaged Kataib Hezbollah withdrawing within a month.
candidates.title: Iraqi forces establish headquarters near Kataib Hezbollah stronghold
